evidence: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Ranunculaceae herbarium index includes three Aquilegia canadensis specimens.
Williamson — dedicated county treatment documents A. canadensis.
Kerr — Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular flora includes a voucher for A. canadensis.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Purola red columbine is introduced and is not counted for Hays range evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with the flower architecture: nodding red-and-yellow flowers have five long backward-pointing nectar spurs, while the leaves are divided into rounded fan-shaped leaflets. In Central Texas, look in shaded limestone canyon bottoms and mesic cliffs.
diagnostic_traits: several erect follicles developing after flowering
